summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was admitted for rectal bleeding and right upper quadrant pain. He presented with bright red blood per rectum followed by black, watery stools and a drop in hemoglobin. Evaluation showed stable cirrhosis without decompensation, no active bleeding on endoscopy, and aphthous ulcers in the rectum and descending colon on colonoscopy, which were likely the source of bleeding. The bleeding resolved during admission, and he remained hemodynamically stable. He was discharged home with a short course of ciprofloxacin, continuation of all home medications, and plans to follow up with his primary care provider and transplant team for biopsy results and further evaluation of possible inflammatory bowel disease.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
